entities.summary: Chợ Rẫy Hospital is the largest general hospital in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam; and is also one of the three high specialized hospital in Vietnam along with Bạch Mai Hospital and Huế Central Hospital, founded in 1900 during the French colonial rule as Hôpital Municipal de Cholon. Over the years, the hospital has also been known as Hôpital Indigène de Cochinchine (1919), Hôpital Lolung Bonnoires (1938), and Hôpital 415 (1945), until it was ultimately renamed Chợ Rẫy in 1957.
